# Model and source

* Citation: Sten S, Cardilin T, Antonsson M, Gennemark P. Plasma Pharmacokinetics of
  N-Acetylgalactosamine-Conjugated Small-Interfering Ribonucleic Acids (GalNAc-Conjugated
  siRNAs). Clin Pharmacokinet. 2023;62(12):1661-1672.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-023-01314-7> (open access, PMC10684612)
* Original mPBPK-PD model: Ayyar VS et al. J Pharmacol Exp Ther. 2021;379(2):134-146.
  <https://doi.org/10.1124/jpet.121.000805>

Sten 2023 pooled published plasma pharmacokinetics of nine GalNAc-conjugated siRNAs and
reported four kinds of model. Three of them are ODE models and are packaged here:

| Model file | What it is | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Sten_2023_givosiran_che`, `Sten_2023_givosiran_aip`, `Sten_2023_vutrisiran`, `Sten_2023_lumasiran_healthy`, `Sten_2023_lumasiran_ph1`, `Sten_2023_olpasiran_1cmt`, `Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalnormal`, `Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalmild`, `Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalmoderate`, `Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalsevere` | Ten independent one-compartment fits (first-order absorption) to the first 24 or 48 h after dose, one per compound and population | ESM Table S4 |
| `Sten_2023_olpasiran_3cmt` | Three-compartment fit to olpasiran alone (data to 12 weeks) | Table 3, column 1 |
| `Sten_2023_galnacSirna_3cmt` | Three-compartment fit with one parameter set shared by inclisiran, givosiran, lumasiran, vutrisiran and olpasiran | Table 3, column 2; Fig. 5 |
| `Sten_2023_fitusiran_mpbpk_mouse`, `_rat`, `_monkey`, `_human` | Ayyar 2021 minimal PBPK-PD model (fitusiran / antithrombin) in the corrected form given as MATLAB code in the ESM, one file per species parameter set | ESM "Implementation of the PBPK model by Ayyar et al."; Fig. 6 |

The fourth kind, the log-log linear regressions of AUC and Cmax on dose and of CL/F on body
weight (Table 2), is a statistical summary rather than an ODE model. It is not packaged, but
it is used below as an independent check on the compartmental models.

All compartmental fits are naive pooled on published group-mean profiles (Phoenix WinNonlin),
so they carry no between-subject variability. Sten 2023 does not report the residual-error
model, so each file carries `propSd = fixed(0)`. Clearances and volumes are apparent
(divided by the unknown bioavailability F). Dose is in mg of siRNA and `Cc` in ng/mL.

# Population

The data are literature means, not individual data. The ESM spreadsheet (sheet
`Time_course_data`) holds 34 mean plasma concentration-time profiles after a single
subcutaneous dose, each the mean or median of 3 to 12 subjects:

* givosiran: three single doses (26.53, 75.8, 189.5 mg) in chronic high excreters (CHE) and two
  dose levels (189.5, 379 mg) in acute intermittent porphyria (AIP) patients with attacks
  (Agarwal 2020; FDA NDA 212194 review), to 24 h;
* vutrisiran: 5-300 mg in healthy volunteers (Habtemariam 2021), to 24 h;
* lumasiran: 21.6-432 mg in healthy volunteers and 50 or 150 mg in primary hyperoxaluria type 1
  (PH1) (Frishberg 2021), to 48 h;
* inclisiran: 300 mg in adults with normal renal function and mild, moderate or severe renal
  impairment (Wright 2020), to 24 h;
* olpasiran: 3-225 mg in adults with elevated lipoprotein(a) (Koren 2022), to 2016 h (12 weeks).

The mPBPK-PD files have no study population: each is a species parameter set (mouse 28 g,
rat 280 g, cynomolgus monkey 6.2 kg, human 71 kg) carried from Ayyar 2021 with the Sten 2023
corrections. The `population` element of each model holds these details.

```{r data}
tc$cohort[is.na(tc$cohort)] <- ""
tc <- tc |>
  mutate(
    model = case_when(
      drug == "givosiran" & cohort == "CHE" ~ "Sten_2023_givosiran_che",
      drug == "givosiran" & cohort == "AIP" ~ "Sten_2023_givosiran_aip",
      drug == "vutrisiran" ~ "Sten_2023_vutrisiran",
      drug == "lumasiran" & cohort == "Healthy" ~ "Sten_2023_lumasiran_healthy",
      drug == "lumasiran" ~ "Sten_2023_lumasiran_ph1",
      drug == "olpasiran" ~ "Sten_2023_olpasiran_1cmt",
      cohort == "normal" ~ "Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalnormal",
      cohort == "mild impairment" ~ "Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalmild",
      cohort == "moderate impairment" ~ "Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalmoderate",
      cohort == "severe impairment" ~ "Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalsevere"
    ),
    # Fit windows of ESM Table S4
    window = ifelse(drug %in% c("lumasiran", "olpasiran"), 48, 24)
  )
nrow(tc)
length(unique(tc$id))
```

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. In summary:

| Model / parameter | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| One-compartment fits: `lka`, `lcl` (CL/F), `lvc` (V/F) | per file | ESM Table S4, the column for that compound and population |
| `Sten_2023_olpasiran_3cmt`: Ka, V1/F, V2/F, V3/F, CL1/F, CL2/F, CL3/F | 0.635 1/h, 27.9, 1470, 296 L, 27.7, 2.62, 914 L/h | Table 3, "Model fitted to olpasiran data only" |
| `Sten_2023_galnacSirna_3cmt`: same parameters | 0.157 1/h, 18.1, 1340, 100 L, 23.8, 3.02, 45.4 L/h | Table 3, "Model simultaneously fitted to all data" |
| Three-compartment mapping | V1 -> `vc`, CL1 -> `cl`, V2/CL2 -> `vp`/`q`, V3/CL3 -> `vp2`/`q2` | Table 3 (Phoenix three-compartment parameterization) |
| `propSd` (all compartmental files) | `fixed(0)` | not reported |
| mPBPK-PD ODEs (18 states) | -- | ESM MATLAB function `Ayyar_mPBPKPD`, `dAa` ... `dProtein` |
| mPBPK-PD parameters (species values) | per file | ESM MATLAB function, `species == 1` to `4` branches |
| Allometric scaling of `kint`, `PS`, `CLuplivin`, `CLupliveff` | `(BW/0.028)^-0.25` and `^0.75` | ESM MATLAB function, rat / monkey / human branches |
| Outputs `Cliver`, `Ckidney`, `Crisc` | -- | ESM figure scripts (`outLiver`, `outKidney`, `outRISC`) |
| Body weights for mg/kg dosing | 0.028, 0.28, 6.2, 71 kg | ESM figure scripts (`BW = ...`) |

# One-compartment fits (ESM Table S4)

Each one-compartment model is simulated at the doses of its own cohort and overlaid on the
mean data it was fitted to. Points beyond the 24 / 48 h fit window (inclisiran and olpasiran
were sampled longer) are not shown.

```{r onecmt-sim}
one_models <- unique(tc$model)
sim_profile <- function(model_name, dose, times) {
  mod <- readModelDb(model_name)
  ev <- et(amt = dose, cmt = "depot") |> et(times)
  out <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame"))
  out[out$time %in% times, c("time", "Cc")]
}
grid1 <- c(seq(0, 2, by = 0.1), seq(2.5, 48, by = 0.5))
pred1 <- tc |>
  distinct(model, id, drug, dose, window) |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(model, id, drug, dose, window, sim_profile(model, dose, grid1)) |>
  filter(time <= window)
obs1 <- filter(tc, time <= window)
```

```{r onecmt-fig, fig.height = 9}
ggplot(obs1, aes(time, conc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = filter(pred1, time > 0), aes(time, Cc, group = id)) +
  facet_wrap(~ sub("Sten_2023_", "", model), ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma siRNA (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose (mg)") +
  theme_bw()
```

The fit of each model to its own data is summarised by the log10 ratio of prediction to
observation:

```{r onecmt-resid}
fit1 <- obs1 |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(model, id, dose) |>
  group_modify(\(x, key) {
    p <- sim_profile(key$model, key$dose, x$time)
    mutate(x, pred = p$Cc[match(x$time, p$time)])
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(lr = log10(pred / conc))
fit1_sum <- fit1 |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    `median log10(pred/obs)` = round(median(lr), 3),
    `median abs log10(pred/obs)` = round(median(abs(lr)), 3)
  )
knitr::kable(fit1_sum)
stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed Ka, CL/F or V/F shifts a whole profile and moves the median
  # log ratio well beyond 0.1 (a 26% bias); every fit is centred on its own data.
  all(abs(fit1_sum$`median log10(pred/obs)`) < 0.1),
  all(fit1_sum$`median abs log10(pred/obs)` < 0.2)
)
```

## NCA of the one-compartment models against the reported exposure

The ESM spreadsheet (sheet `AUC_Cmax`) also lists the reported Cmax and AUC of the cohorts
behind these profiles. The one-compartment models are simulated at those doses and analysed
with PKNCA. AUC0-inf of a linear one-compartment model equals Dose/(CL/F) exactly, which is
also checked.

```{r onecmt-nca}
ref1 <- tribble(
  ~model, ~dose, ~aucinf.obs, ~cmax,
  "Sten_2023_vutrisiran", 5, 131, 19.6,
  "Sten_2023_vutrisiran", 25, 1020, 87.5,
  "Sten_2023_vutrisiran", 50, 2180, 178,
  "Sten_2023_vutrisiran", 100, 5200, 396,
  "Sten_2023_vutrisiran", 200, 12700, 727,
  "Sten_2023_vutrisiran", 300, 15500, 1090,
  "Sten_2023_lumasiran_healthy", 21.6, 294, 39.8,
  "Sten_2023_lumasiran_healthy", 72, 1900, 204,
  "Sten_2023_lumasiran_healthy", 216, 7210, 534,
  "Sten_2023_lumasiran_healthy", 432, 16800, 1180,
  "Sten_2023_givosiran_che", 26.53, 293, 52.1,
  "Sten_2023_givosiran_che", 75.8, 1180, 124,
  "Sten_2023_givosiran_che", 189.5, 4620, 356,
  "Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalnormal", 300, 7890, 421,
  "Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalmild", 300, 11600, 987,
  "Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalmoderate", 300, 10800, 897,
  "Sten_2023_inclisiran_renalsevere", 300, 18800, 1760
) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(sub("Sten_2023_", "", model), dose, "mg"))

grid_nca <- c(seq(0, 12, by = 0.25), seq(13, 48, by = 1), seq(50, 240, by = 2))
conc1 <- ref1 |>
  rowwise() |>
  reframe(treatment, model, dose, sim_profile(model, dose, grid_nca)) |>
  mutate(id = 1L) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))
dose1 <- distinct(conc1, treatment, id, dose) |> mutate(time = 0)
o_conc <- PKNCAconc(conc1, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
o_dose <- PKNCAdose(dose1, dose ~ time | treatment + id)
o_data <- PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
)
nca1 <- as.data.frame(pk.nca(o_data))
tbl1 <- ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca1,
  reference = select(ref1, treatment, aucinf.obs, cmax),
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "h*ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 50
)
knitr::kable(tbl1, caption = attr(tbl1, "footnote"))

# Closed form: AUC0-inf = 1000 * Dose / (CL/F) in h*ng/mL.
cl_of <- function(m) exp(unname(readModelDb(m)()$theta["lcl"]))
auc_check <- nca1 |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(distinct(ref1, treatment, model, dose), by = "treatment") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(closed = 1000 * dose / cl_of(model)) |>
  ungroup()
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_check$PPORRES / auc_check$closed - 1) < 0.01))
```

The one-compartment models, fitted to the first 24-48 h only, reproduce the reported Cmax of
every cohort within about 25%. The inclisiran reported AUC0-inf rises with renal impairment
(7890 to 18800 h*ng/mL) and the per-population CL/F of Table S4 falls in the same order (35.6
to 17.0 L/h). The rows flagged with a star (more than 50% difference) are the lowest doses of
vutrisiran, lumasiran and givosiran. Within each of those cohorts the reported dose-normalised
AUC rises with dose (vutrisiran 26 h*ng/mL per mg at 5 mg against 52-64 at 100-300 mg), which
one linear model per population, fitted to all doses at once, cannot follow; the closed-form
check above confirms the models themselves are transcribed exactly.

# Three-compartment models (Table 3, Fig. 5, ESM Fig. S1)

```{r threecmt-sim}
# The observed sampling times are added so every observation has a prediction.
grid3 <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.5), seq(50, 2016, by = 4), tc$time)))
pred3 <- bind_rows(lapply(
  c("Sten_2023_galnacSirna_3cmt", "Sten_2023_olpasiran_3cmt"),
  function(m) {
    tc |>
      distinct(id, drug, dose) |>
      rowwise() |>
      reframe(id, drug, dose, sim_profile(m, dose, grid3)) |>
      mutate(fit = m)
  }
))
```

```{r threecmt-fig5, fig.height = 7}
obs_mean <- tc |>
  group_by(drug, dose, time) |>
  summarise(conc = mean(conc), .groups = "drop")
pred3_mean <- pred3 |>
  distinct(fit, drug, dose, time, Cc) |>
  filter(time > 0)
ggplot(filter(obs_mean, time <= 168), aes(time, conc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(
    data = filter(pred3_mean, fit == "Sten_2023_galnacSirna_3cmt", time <= 168),
    aes(time, Cc)
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma siRNA (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose (mg)",
    title = "Joint three-compartment fit (lines) and mean data (points)"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figure 5 of Sten 2023 (first week); the olpasiran 12-week panel follows.

```{r threecmt-olpasiran}
ggplot(filter(obs_mean, drug == "olpasiran"), aes(time / 24, conc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = filter(pred3_mean, drug == "olpasiran"), aes(time / 24, Cc, linetype = fit)) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = "Time (days)", y = "Plasma olpasiran (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose (mg)", linetype = NULL,
    title = "Olpasiran: joint fit and olpasiran-only fit"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

The olpasiran-only and joint fits agree for the first two days and both carry the long
terminal phase (V2/F of 1470 and 1340 L) that Fig. 5 shows at 12 weeks.

```{r threecmt-resid}
fit3 <- pred3 |>
  inner_join(filter(tc, time > 0), by = c("id", "drug", "dose", "time")) |>
  mutate(lr = log10(Cc / conc))
fit3_sum <- bind_rows(
  fit3 |> filter(fit == "Sten_2023_galnacSirna_3cmt") |> group_by(fit, drug) |>
    summarise(n = n(), med = median(lr), mad = median(abs(lr)), .groups = "drop"),
  fit3 |> filter(fit == "Sten_2023_olpasiran_3cmt", drug == "olpasiran") |> group_by(fit, drug) |>
    summarise(n = n(), med = median(lr), mad = median(abs(lr)), .groups = "drop")
) |>
  mutate(across(c(med, mad), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  rename(`median log10(pred/obs)` = med, `median abs log10(pred/obs)` = mad)
knitr::kable(fit3_sum)
stopifnot(
  # The joint fit is one parameter set for five compounds, so per-compound bias up to
  # about 0.2 log10 (1.6-fold) is inside the twofold band Sten 2023 report around the
  # class-level regressions; a swapped V2/V3 or CL2/CL3 pair moves it far beyond this.
  all(abs(fit3_sum$`median log10(pred/obs)`) < 0.25),
  all(fit3_sum$`median abs log10(pred/obs)` < 0.25)
)
```

## NCA of the joint model against the dose-exposure regressions (Table 2)

Table 2 reports class-level regressions in humans, AUC = 10^1.45 x Dose^1.05 and
Cmax = 10^0.470 x Dose^0.989 (Dose in mg, AUC in h*ng/mL, Cmax in ng/mL), with a twofold band
covering most of the data. The joint three-compartment model should fall inside that band.

```{r threecmt-nca}
doses_nca <- c(25, 100, 300)
grid_long <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), seq(25, 168, by = 1), seq(170, 4032, by = 8))))
conc3 <- bind_rows(lapply(doses_nca, function(d) {
  sim_profile("Sten_2023_galnacSirna_3cmt", d, grid_long) |>
    mutate(treatment = paste(d, "mg"), dose = d, id = 1L)
}))
d3 <- distinct(conc3, treatment, id, dose) |> mutate(time = 0)
nca3 <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(
  PKNCAconc(conc3, Cc ~ time | treatment + id),
  PKNCAdose(d3, dose ~ time | treatment + id),
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE)
))
ref3 <- data.frame(
  treatment = paste(doses_nca, "mg"),
  aucinf.obs = 10^1.45 * doses_nca^1.05,
  cmax = 10^0.470 * doses_nca^0.989
)
tbl3 <- ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = as.data.frame(nca3),
  reference = ref3,
  by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "aucinf.obs"),
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "h*ng/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 100
)
knitr::kable(tbl3, caption = attr(tbl3, "footnote"))
sim3 <- as.data.frame(nca3) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  left_join(pivot_longer(ref3, -treatment, names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("treatment", "PPTESTCD")
  )
stopifnot(all(sim3$PPORRES / sim3$ref > 0.5 & sim3$PPORRES / sim3$ref < 2))
```

The terminal half-life of the joint model follows from its smallest eigenvalue:

```{r threecmt-thalf}
th <- function(m) {
  p <- exp(readModelDb(m)()$theta)
  k <- matrix(c(
    -(p[["lcl"]] + p[["lq"]] + p[["lq2"]]) / p[["lvc"]], p[["lq"]] / p[["lvp"]], p[["lq2"]] / p[["lvp2"]],
    p[["lq"]] / p[["lvc"]], -p[["lq"]] / p[["lvp"]], 0,
    p[["lq2"]] / p[["lvc"]], 0, -p[["lq2"]] / p[["lvp2"]]
  ), 3, byrow = TRUE)
  log(2) / min(abs(eigen(k)$values)) / 24
}
c(joint_days = th("Sten_2023_galnacSirna_3cmt"), olpasiran_only_days = th("Sten_2023_olpasiran_3cmt"))
```

Both fits give a terminal plasma half-life of several weeks, the redistribution-driven phase
the abstract describes.

# Corrected Ayyar 2021 mPBPK-PD model (ESM)

The ESM gives MATLAB scripts that regenerate Ayyar 2021 Figs. 2-5 with the corrected model
and shows their output. The packaged models are simulated with the same doses, and the
extremes the maintainers read off the ESM panels are checked below (deterministic model, so
the comparison is exact up to the reading precision of the plots).

```{r pbpk-helper}
pbpk_run <- function(species, bw, mgkg, tend, dose_times = 0) {
  mod <- readModelDb(paste0("Sten_2023_fitusiran_mpbpk_", species))
  bind_rows(lapply(mgkg, function(d) {
    ev <- et(amt = d * bw, cmt = "depot", time = dose_times) |> et(seq(0, tend, by = 1))
    as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev, atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8, returnType = "data.frame")) |>
      mutate(dose_mgkg = d)
  }))
}
nadir <- function(sim) {
  sim |>
    group_by(dose_mgkg) |>
    summarise(
      mrna_min = min(mrna_liver), t_mrna = time[which.min(mrna_liver)],
      protein_min = min(protein), t_protein = time[which.min(protein)],
      risc_max = max(Crisc), t_risc = time[which.max(Crisc)],
      liver_max = max(Cliver)
    )
}
```

## Mouse (Ayyar 2021 Fig. 2; 1, 2.5 and 5 mg/kg SC)

```{r pbpk-mouse}
s_mouse <- pbpk_run("mouse", 0.028, c(1, 2.5, 5), 1000)
n_mouse <- nadir(s_mouse)
knitr::kable(n_mouse, digits = 2)
s_mouse |>
  select(time, dose_mgkg, `Liver (ng/g)` = Cliver, `RISC-bound (ng/g)` = Crisc,
    `Liver mRNA (%)` = mrna_liver, `Plasma protein (%)` = protein) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(time, dose_mgkg)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = factor(dose_mgkg))) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = NULL, colour = "Dose (mg/kg)") +
  theme_bw()
# Read from the ESM panels: mRNA nadir ~48 / ~29 / ~20 %, protein nadir ~34 / ~16 / ~9 %,
# RISC-bound peak ~3.2 ng/g near 140 h at 2.5 mg/kg.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(n_mouse$mrna_min / c(48, 29, 20) - 1) < 0.1),
  all(abs(n_mouse$protein_min / c(34, 16, 9) - 1) < 0.15),
  abs(n_mouse$risc_max[2] / 3.2 - 1) < 0.1
)
```

## Rat (Ayyar 2021 Fig. 3; 1, 5 and 10 mg/kg SC)

```{r pbpk-rat}
s_rat <- pbpk_run("rat", 0.28, c(1, 5, 10), 700)
n_rat <- nadir(s_rat)
knitr::kable(n_rat, digits = 2)
# Read from the ESM panels: RISC-bound peak ~1.2 ng/g (1 mg/kg) and ~5.6 ng/g (5 mg/kg);
# 10 mg/kg liver concentration peaks just under 1e5 ng/g and is ~1e4 ng/g at 300 h.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(n_rat$risc_max[1:2] / c(1.2, 5.6) - 1) < 0.1),
  n_rat$liver_max[3] > 5e4 && n_rat$liver_max[3] < 1e5,
  abs(log10(s_rat$Cliver[s_rat$dose_mgkg == 10 & s_rat$time == 300] / 1e4)) < 0.15
)
```

## Cynomolgus monkey (Ayyar 2021 Fig. 4; 1, 3, 10 and 30 mg/kg SC)

```{r pbpk-monkey}
s_monkey <- pbpk_run("monkey", 6.2, c(1, 3, 10, 30), 1500)
n_monkey <- nadir(s_monkey)
knitr::kable(n_monkey, digits = 2)
ggplot(s_monkey, aes(time, protein, colour = factor(dose_mgkg))) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma antithrombin (%)", colour = "Dose (mg/kg)") +
  theme_bw()
# Read from the ESM panel: nadirs ~47, ~24, ~10.5 and ~5.3 % at ~310, ~365, ~480, ~690 h.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(n_monkey$protein_min / c(47, 24, 10.5, 5.3) - 1) < 0.1),
  all(abs(n_monkey$t_protein / c(310, 365, 480, 690) - 1) < 0.1)
)
```

## Human (Ayyar 2021 Fig. 5)

Three monthly doses of 80 mg or 0.225 mg/kg, three weekly doses of 0.015 mg/kg, a single dose
of 0.03 mg/kg (Fig. 5B) and three monthly doses of 1.8 or 0.45 mg/kg (Fig. 5C), in a 71 kg
adult.

```{r pbpk-human}
q4w <- c(0, 28, 56) * 24
s_h <- bind_rows(
  pbpk_run("human", 71, c(80 / 71, 0.225, 1.8, 0.45), 6000, q4w) |> mutate(regimen = "Q4W x3"),
  pbpk_run("human", 71, 0.015, 6000, c(0, 7, 14) * 24) |> mutate(regimen = "QW x3"),
  pbpk_run("human", 71, 0.03, 6000) |> mutate(regimen = "single")
) |>
  mutate(label = paste(signif(dose_mgkg, 3), "mg/kg", regimen))
n_h <- s_h |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(protein_min = min(protein), t_protein = time[which.min(protein)])
knitr::kable(n_h, digits = 2)
ggplot(s_h, aes(time, protein, colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma antithrombin (%)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
nh <- setNames(n_h$protein_min, n_h$label)
# Read from the ESM panels: nadirs ~9.5 (80 mg), ~35 (0.225 mg/kg), ~6.5 (1.8 mg/kg),
# ~20.5 (0.45 mg/kg), ~87 (0.015 mg/kg QW) and ~90.5 % (0.03 mg/kg single).
stopifnot(
  abs(nh[["1.13 mg/kg Q4W x3"]] / 9.5 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(nh[["0.225 mg/kg Q4W x3"]] / 35 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(nh[["1.8 mg/kg Q4W x3"]] / 6.5 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(nh[["0.45 mg/kg Q4W x3"]] / 20.5 - 1) < 0.1,
  abs(nh[["0.015 mg/kg QW x3"]] - 87) < 3,
  abs(nh[["0.03 mg/kg single"]] - 90.5) < 3
)
```

## Olpasiran plasma profile with the human mPBPK model (Fig. 6)

Sten 2023 Fig. 6 compares the human parameter set with the olpasiran data: it captures the
first days but falls well below the observed concentrations beyond 168 h. The same comparison,
with the mPBPK model and the joint three-compartment model side by side:

```{r pbpk-fig6}
olp_doses <- c(3, 9, 30, 75, 225)
grid6 <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 48, by = 0.5), seq(50, 2016, by = 4))))
p6 <- bind_rows(lapply(olp_doses, function(d) {
  mod <- readModelDb("Sten_2023_fitusiran_mpbpk_human")
  out <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, et(amt = d, cmt = "depot") |> et(grid6),
    atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-8, returnType = "data.frame"
  ))
  data.frame(dose = d, time = out$time, Cc = out$Cc, model = "mPBPK (human)")
}))
p6 <- bind_rows(
  p6,
  pred3_mean |>
    filter(fit == "Sten_2023_galnacSirna_3cmt", drug == "olpasiran") |>
    transmute(dose, time, Cc, model = "joint three-compartment")
)
ggplot(filter(obs_mean, drug == "olpasiran", time <= 336), aes(time, conc, colour = factor(dose))) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line(data = filter(p6, time > 0, time <= 336), aes(time, Cc, linetype = model)) +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(1e-3, 1e3)) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma olpasiran (ng/mL)", colour = "Dose (mg)", linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
v6 <- filter(p6, model == "mPBPK (human)", dose == 225, time %in% c(168, 336))
# Read from Sten 2023 Fig. 6 (225 mg line): ~0.2 ng/mL at 168 h and ~0.006 ng/mL at 336 h.
stopifnot(
  abs(log10(v6$Cc[v6$time == 168] / 0.2)) < 0.15,
  abs(log10(v6$Cc[v6$time == 336] / 0.006)) < 0.15
)
```

## Baseline steady state

Without a dose every receptor, mRNA and protein state must stay at its baseline
(free ASGPR = Rtot because ksyn = Rtot x kdeg, correction 4 of the ESM).

```{r pbpk-steady}
ss <- bind_rows(lapply(c("mouse", "rat", "monkey", "human"), function(sp) {
  mod <- readModelDb(paste0("Sten_2023_fitusiran_mpbpk_", sp))
  th <- mod()$theta
  out <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, et(seq(0, 2000, by = 500)), returnType = "data.frame"))
  data.frame(
    species = sp,
    target_dev = max(abs(out$target / th[["rtot"]] - 1)),
    mrna_dev = max(abs(out$mrna_liver / th[["mrna0"]] - 1)),
    protein_dev = max(abs(out$protein / th[["protein0"]] - 1))
  )
}))
knitr::kable(ss, digits = 12)
stopifnot(all(as.matrix(ss[, -1]) < 1e-8))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Residual error.** Sten 2023 does not report the residual-error model of the WinNonlin
  naive-pooled fits, so the compartmental files carry `propSd = fixed(0)`. They are
  typical-value (group-mean) models and should not be used to simulate between-subject
  variability.
* **Naive pooling.** The population sizes in each `population` element are the sums of the
  per-arm group sizes the ESM spreadsheet lists for the cohorts behind the profiles; the
  fits themselves used only the group means. For the joint three-compartment model the
  subject count is left unset.
* **One-compartment files are per population, not a covariate model.** Sten 2023 fitted each
  compound / population separately (Table S4); the files reproduce that structure instead of
  combining, for example, the four inclisiran renal-function fits into one model with renal
  indicators.
* **mPBPK-PD units.** The ESM code doses the depot in ng; the packaged models take the dose in
  mg and convert (x 1e6) where the depot feeds plasma. The other states keep the units of the
  ESM code (plasma, remainder, kidney vascular and liver vascular in ng/mL, kidney tissue in
  ng/g, kidney bound pool in ng, liver bound pool in nmol, receptor and intracellular states in
  nM, mRNA and protein in percent of baseline), so they are concentrations rather than amounts.
* **mPBPK-PD body weight.** The allometric scaling and mg/kg dosing use one typical weight per
  species (`bw`, a fixed parameter), as in the ESM scripts. Simulating another animal size
  means changing `bw` (and the physiological volumes and flows, which the ESM gives only for
  these four weights).
* **SC50 unit.** The mouse and rat branches of the ESM code print the SC50 unit as "ng/M"; it
  is compared with the RISC-bound siRNA concentration in nM and is treated as nM.
* **Rat PD parameters.** The ESM marks the rat kdeg_mRNA, kdeg_protein, Smax, SC50 and gamma
  as not available in Ayyar 2021 and carries the mouse values; the packaged rat file does the
  same.
* **Monkey baseline protein.** The monkey parameter set uses protein0 = 110% (assigned by
  Sten 2023 from Ayyar 2021 Fig. 4); the steady-state check above uses this baseline.
* **Drug name of the mPBPK-PD files.** The model is a generic GalNAc-siRNA framework, but its PD
  layer (antithrombin mRNA and protein) and calibration come from fitusiran, so the files are
  named for fitusiran. Sten 2023 applies the human parameter set to olpasiran plasma data
  only (Fig. 6), as above.
* **Table 2 regressions** are statistical summaries and are not packaged; they are used only as
  an external check on the joint three-compartment model.
* **Figure read-offs.** The PBPK check values are read by the maintainers from the panels the
  ESM prints for its own MATLAB runs; tolerances (10-15%, or 0.15 log10 for the log-scale
  plasma values) reflect the reading precision of those plots.
